history.summary: The best-documented 'Ram Janki Mandir' matching this CSV row is the Shree Ram Janki Mandir on Sohela-Baramkela Road at Baramkela, Chhattisgarh (reviewed on vimarsana), a temple dedicated to Lord Rama and Goddess Sita with idols of Rama, Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman in traditional North Indian temple style, and a focal point for Ram Navami celebrations. TOWN CORRECTION: the temple is at Baramkela, not in Raigarh town - about 35 km south of Raigarh city. DISTRICT NOTE: Baramkela now lies in Sarangarh-Bilaigarh district (carved out in 2022), not Raigarh district. COORDINATE CONFLICT: vimarsana reports 21.4937633, 83.2957958 for this temple, which conflicts with Baramkela town (21.56634, 83.26202); town-level coordinates are used here and marked approximate. No founding date is documented online.

name: Shree Ram Janki Mandir
town_description: Baramkela is a town on the Sohela-Baramkela road in Sarangarh-Bilaigarh district of Chhattisgarh, a local market centre for surrounding agricultural villages between Raigarh and Sarangarh.

travel.airport: Swami Vivekananda Airport, Raipur (~250 km) is the nearest major airport
travel.road: Sohela-Baramkela Road; Baramkela lies on the Raigarh-Sarangarh route

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Ram Navami is the major festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open all days, mostly 9:30 AM to 8:30 PM (review-site reported; call ahead to confirm)
